vectorization_witnesses.note: report 10 delta 2. Deterministic, so it gates: a loop that stops vectorizing fails here before wall time moves on the current machine. `wolf` counts remarks from `clang -x ir -O2` on the module the backend actually emits; `c_naive` from `clang -O3` on ref.c. A wolf count of 0 across the board was the s44 finding, not the s44 target — the floors were recorded so the first kernel that started vectorizing would be visible. s75 is that moment: `alias_daxpy` vectorizes now that element access is `ptr.off` + `load` instead of a runtime call, and its floor ratchets to 1. s85 is the second: `e1_sum_reduce` vectorizes because its overflow check is GONE — proven away by the trip-scaled accumulator bound, not switched off — which is the falsifiable form of D44's claim that the check was the only thing stopping LoopVectorize. Its floor ratchets to 1, so a range analysis that regresses fails here rather than in a nightly wall number. The rest stay at 0 with a reason each, in bench/loss-ledger.md: `aos_dot` is a float reduction LLVM will not reassociate, `a2_stencil1d` still carries a bounds guard the relational analysis cannot discharge (`i <u out.len` against a loop guarded by `src.len - 1`, and the program never relates the two lengths, so no closure over the known relations can decide it — it wants a version guard on the invariant PAIR, wolf-lang#98) plus two overflow traps on `int` elements that carry no width bound, `a5_hoist_call` was redesigned for #97 (the callee WRITES memory now, so the fold is impossible by construction): its c_naive floor drops 1 -> 0 because the may-alias store is exactly what forbids clang to vectorize — a naive lane that starts vectorizing this kernel again means the aliasing hazard has been optimized away and the kernel has stopped measuring its thesis, so 0 is the honest floor on BOTH sides; the serial scratch chain keeps even expert C scalar. s99: a2's wolf floor 0 -> 1 — the interprocedural container channel proves src's elements [0,255], the element-sum chks discharge, and the versioned fast loop vectorizes for the first time (2 remarks observed at clang 22.1.8: the fast copy's main and epilogue; floor 1 is the rot-proof minimum across toolchains). s101 adds `align16_min`: a floor on `!align` buffer-pointer claims in the emitted wolf module — the alignment FACT (ChunkBlock's repr(align(16)) base + 16-grained grants) pinned in the IR so it cannot silently degrade; the measured outcome it licenses is recorded in G9 (one window load aligned + two folded, memory-port count unchanged — cross-iteration carry is the named residue, s102's). s104 adds `noalias_pair_scopes_min`: a floor on the guarded-noalias pair scope definitions ({fn}.pairN.a/b) in the emitted wolf module — the versioner's runtime buffer-overlap guard proves disjointness on its taken edge, the fact rides `: guard` custody, and the emitter splits the Foreign(Buffer) class per pair (the split #82 refused statically; the guard is the runtime complement). a2_stencil1d and alias_daxpy both mint one pair (floor 2 = both halves). The outcome it licenses, measured at clang 22.1.8 on this host: a2's fast loop 5 loads + 2 stores -> 3 loads + 2 stores per 4 outputs (2 movaps + 1 folded paddq), the +1 window carried across the backedge in a register (pshufd splice) — the cross-iteration carry s102 named as the residue, landed. Three ingredients, all load-bearing and all measured by ablation: the pair split with the class scope OUT of the members' alias.scope (one stray class scope makes scoped-noalias inert), s101's 16-align claim (movaps), and the typed-GEP stride spelling (LLVM's vectorizer declines the carry on mul + byte-GEP addressing, identical SCEVs notwithstanding).
